USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Bleeding complication

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 55-year-old patient with a history of ulcer disease presents with black tarry stools, dizziness and tachycardia. He is not taking bismuth or iron. Which complication is most important to assess urgently in this presentation?

  1. Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
  2. Uncomplicated acid reflux alone
  3. Simple dietary stool discoloration
  4. Isolated lactose intolerance
  5. An asymptomatic healed ulcer
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Upper gastrointestinal bleeding

Melena with circulatory symptoms raises concern for significant GI blood loss.

Understanding the options

Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
Melena with circulatory symptoms raises concern for significant GI blood loss.
Uncomplicated acid reflux alone
This does not explain melena with hemodynamic symptoms.
Simple dietary stool discoloration
The tarry stool and systemic findings are concerning for bleeding.
Isolated lactose intolerance
This does not characteristically cause melena.
An asymptomatic healed ulcer
The current symptoms suggest an active complication.
